scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: An electric car has no engine, no fuel tank, and no gears to shift. So what's really moving it?

scenes.name: pack
scenes.text: Under the floor sits a battery pack. Hundreds, or even thousands, of lithium ion cells, wired together.

scenes.name: ions
scenes.text: Each cell has two sides. As you drive, lithium ions flow from one side to the other inside the cell, and electrons flow out through the wires.

scenes.name: inv
scenes.text: That current is DC. An inverter turns it into AC, at the exact frequency the motor needs.

scenes.name: motor
scenes.text: In the motor, changing magnetic fields spin the rotor, which turns the wheels. Strong torque, almost instantly.

scenes.name: regen
scenes.text: When you slow down, the motor works as a generator, sending energy back into the battery.

scenes.name: bms
scenes.text: A battery management system watches every cell's voltage and temperature, while cooling keeps the pack in its comfort zone.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Cells, inverter, motor, regen. Electricity in motion. Follow for more on how things really work.
